s5.conf: medium - by far the most complex image (~90 heavy atoms, 6 stereocenters, 12-membered tetraaza macrocycle). Connectivity was cross-verified extensively (pixel-cluster heteroatom mapping plus dozens of targeted crops, chain lengths counted more than once each). All 6 stereocenters were built from locally-observed wedge/hash geometry and I manually re-verified the circular substituent order at each center matched the source drawing, but given the scale of this structure some risk of a local error remains higher than for the other 9 images
medium (connectivity/constitution high confidence; exact wedge/dash at the C8/C9/C14 ring-fusion cluster is lower confidence due to extreme crowding in the source drawing)
medium-high (constitution/connectivity high confidence; ring B/C stereocenters verified directly from clear zoomed crops)
low-medium (connectivity medium-high; stereochemistry not resolved/left unspecified)

n/a - image contains only an isolated double-bond-to-oxygen fragment (two parallel lines meeting a single O atom); the carbon-side end of the bond dangles into blank space with no vertex, no other atom, and no further connectivity anywhere in the file. Verified via pixel bounding-box and full color-palette scan -- nothing else is drawn. No molecule can be determined from this.

medium (connectivity cross-checked by OSRA fragments and an RDKit re-render compared side-by-side with the source image; stereochemistry at the 9 centres was not confidently resolved from the wedges and is omitted)

low - the 3D wireframe projection has extensive overlapping front/back edges that cannot be traced bond-by-bond with confidence, and I have no verified way to reproduce C70's exact ring-closure SMILES without risking a fabricated topology, so I am not providing a specific SMILES

medium (ring size, pentaene count and general topology confirmed by multiple independent crop re-reads and an RDKit re-render; exact CH2-spacer counts in the crowded polyol/branch region are less certain, stereochemistry not assigned)

fable.what: One image (cethromycin, CID 156417, the corpus drawing) read blind by Claude Fable 5.1 and re-read by Sonnet 5.5, same prompt, same sandbox, one image per reader. Scored with sonnet_batch.verdict().

price.note: Sonnet 5.5 and Sonnet 5 list at the same per-token prices.

protocol.why: Cost. A ten-image reader re-reads its whole growing context on every step, so a batch of heavy molecules snowballs: one Sonnet 5.5 reader on ten large gap molecules cost $11.06 (35M cache-read tokens, 144 tool calls) against a $2.30 estimate. One image per reader caps that, lets the cadence predict each reader's cost from the molecule's size, and lets it stop a runaway reader without losing nine other readings.
protocol.prompt_change: The single-image prompts are the arms' ten-image prompts with only the image count changed: 'reading one chemical structure image ... the molecule it depicts', 'The image is:', 'Read the image yourself', 'Write the one entry, fig01'. Every other word, both integrity paragraphs, the sandbox, the exact-model check and the gate are unchanged.
protocol.pairing: From this switch, while both arms were reading, each new image was read by both in its own single-image reader, Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 5.5 started together, so each pair completed together. The rows before it were read ten to a reader, with batch-mates in the same context.
protocol.text: Single-image readers from row 1071 of the Sonnet 5.5 arm and row 1077 of the Sonnet 5 arm (2026-10-02): one image per reader; until Sonnet 5 stopped (2026-10-04) both models read each new image at the same time. Earlier rows were read 10 images to a reader, in one shared context.
